lldp.title: LLDP
lldp.intro: Link Layer Discovery Protocol: advertise this router on its interfaces and see the neighbour heard on each.
lldp.globalsNote: System name, TX hold and TX interval are VPP-wide settings: only the product agent that owns the VPP-global settings applies them. On a lab slot they are reported as not applied and VPP keeps its values. An empty system name keeps VPP's current one.
lldp.indexNote: VPP 26.06 enables LLDP by the hardware interface index. On an interface whose software and hardware indexes differ (anything created after start-up, such as loopbacks) LLDP may be enabled on ANOTHER interface; the agent then reports an error but cannot undo it until VPP restarts. Use LLDP on the interfaces created at start-up (the data NICs).

mirror.title: Port mirroring
mirror.intro: Copy the traffic of a source interface to a destination interface (SPAN). For ERSPAN, choose a GRE tunnel of type erspan as the destination. Every session is kept on the source interface.
mirror.help: The destination must be another interface that is not mirrored itself. Level device copies every frame; level L2 only frames of a bridge member or cross-connect.
mirror.sourceHelp: The interface whose traffic is copied

nsim.title: Network delay simulator
nsim.intro: Adds delay, a bandwidth limit and random loss between two interfaces or on the output of interfaces (VPP nsim). For lab tests only.
nsim.warning: The simulator is VPP-wide and a lab tool: it is applied only by the agent that owns the VPP-global settings AND runs with VRX_NSIM=lab (the API refuses a commit with it otherwise, 409). On a VPP with worker threads it needs `nsim { poll-main-thread }` in startup.conf. Configuring it keeps VPP's main thread polling (a busy core) until VPP restarts; VPP cannot read it back or unconfigure it — removing it here only detaches the interfaces.
